THE EVENING STANDARD
A MYSTERY WOMAN
(Continued from Page 1.)
gave up trying, and dismissed them by giving each a pile of propaganda literature. As Price left the building he saw and recognised a British soldier from Archangel, who was carrying a bundle of papers, and appeared to be employed in a clerical capacity.

SPECIAL MESSENGERS.
WON'T TRUST THE POST.
While the authorities are doing their best to strangle the propagation of Bolshevist doctrine in this country they are naturally confronted with many difficulties.
The Bolshevists, seeking to permeate with their pernicious doctrines the labour classes of this country, do not make use, for obvious reasons, of the ordinary channels of communications such as the post and telegraphs, but invariably endeavour to send special messengers backwards and forwards from the Continent to England.
"The other day," said the high official, "we got information that a certain number of people came over as stowaways from Rotterdam with the collusion of the crew of the ship, who were to get £5 in each case."
Found in the East End.
"We managed to recover about eleven of these men, whom we found in the East End of London.
"They were all people who knew they could not get a passport, and they were sent over by a Jewish organisation in Rotterdam, which tries to assist people in evading the passport regulations.
"We also know that the chief Bolshevists in Russia and Hungary have been trying lately to introduce agents into this country. It would be useless to say that we are always able to find them before they land, and we sometimes obtain knowledge of the fact only after certain Bolshevist material has been disseminated broadcast and brought to our notice.
Organisation in London.
"There is a certain organisation in London which assists in spreading these revolutionary views which are brought from abroad. We sometimes make the discovery in the form of a leaflet which somebody unknown has circulated, or it appears in the circulars of certain organisations of extremist tendencies.
"We have also got information after certain people have got in and got out of this country as stowaways. The only alternative to the present position would be to put on so stringent an examination at the ports that we could restrict travelling, and so speedily ruin these individuals to earth.
"But you cannot at this juncture put a very large check on travelling without doing damage to the interests of the country. People write and say 'Why don't the police stop all this,' but it is not so easy under present conditions.
"Another common practice is to endeavour to employ as a messenger a seaman on a boat running to this country.
"Have you got the situation well in hand?" asked the "Evening Standard" interviewer.
"The people who have got the situation in hand are the British public, who always decide right when they know the facts," was the reply.

REDS' CHANCE NOW.
NEVER HAS SITUATION BEEN SO REVOLUTIONARY.
"The situation has never been so profoundly revolutionary, and there has never been an opportunity so favourable as the present for building up a new world." So declared Gorki, the Russian writer, recently, voicing what is undoubtedly the feeling of Communists, who see in the present chaos and disorganisation of Europe their chance.

A MYSTERY WOMAN.
CHIEF OF THE BOLSHEVIST SYSTEM OF PROPAGANDA.
CONSPIRACY IN RUSSIA.
STORY OF INTRIGUES AMONG BRITISH PRISONERS.
Day by day the widespread character of the Bolshevist plot to ensnare Europe, and particularly Britain, within the insidious toils of the "Red" revolutionaries is being revealed.
To-day the "Evening Standard" is able to place before its readers irrefutable evidence of the great conspiracy, which is practically world-wide. The facts have been obtained from one of the highest officials at Scotland Yard, whose knowledge of the situation is first-hand and whose facts are thoroughly established.
"It is extraordinarily difficult to catch these Bolshevist emissaries," said a high official to-day. "There has been a great outcry that passports and port restrictions are strangling British trade. There is a great deal of truth in that.
"While the traffic to and from the Continent daily is now very great, it is almost impossible to stop, search, and cross-examine everyone, as we are not now in a state of war.
"Even in the case of the most apparently reputable travellers it is always possible to carry a few hundred pound notes in their pockets or lining and satisfactorily account for their possession of the money and its ultimate disposition; but when we have knowledge of certain people coming in, as in the case of the young man from Norway, we are on the look-out for them, and act accordingly."

BOLSHEVISTS TRIED TO BRIBE SERGEANT
OFFERED GOOD PAY IF HE WOULD SPREAD THEIR DOCTRINES.
Details have already been disclosed how the young Norwegian Zachariassen managed to elude the watch at the ports and to place £6000 at the service of the revolutionaries. Ostensibly he was coming over to study social conditions, and posed as a journalist representing a Norwegian paper.
The fact, however, remains that his first calls were on persons of extreme views, and, in one particular instance, on a person whose revolutionary tendencies are un-concealed. In addition, he carried a number of addresses of persons suspected of German espionage during the war.
From the Chief Bolshevik Centre.
But it ought to be made clear that these names does not include those of any Labour leaders in this country, or, in fact, any responsible person. The fact that he came from the chief Bolshevik centre in Norway was, however, sufficient indication of the general purport of his mission.
Then there is the revelation of the discovery of the "Programme of the Central Workers' Soviet Committee," which among its fifteen points, set out as the third: "The army of the entire labour population was a Red Army," and concluded with "Long Live

and Russia itself, under the direct orders of Lenin and Trotsky.
Unfortunately she has not yet risked an attempt to enter this country, which from the point of view of the authorities, is a pity. But she is known as one of the most violent of the "Reds," and it is already known that some of the women in the Russian revolution have been more bloodthirsty and dangerous than the men.
The Bolshevists work in devious ways, and in order to further their nefarious schemes have even gone the length of endeavouring to suborn British prisoners in Russia.

SERGEANT'S STATEMENT
ATTEMPT TO MAKE HIM A BOLSHEVIST AGENT.
The authorities, the "Evening Standard" learns, have just come into possession of the sworn statement of Sergeant Price, of the Machine Gun Corps, who, while a prisoner of war in Russia, was by bribes and promises of advancement, asked to become a Bolshevist agent in England. The statement of Sergeant Price is as follows:—
At the beginning of May last I was working as a labourer, and whilst he was taken before a man named Levine, a Jew.
Price was confronted with some written matter, and asked if proposed had been made to him to go back to England. He freely admitted that he had been approached by the Bolshevists, among which he noticed some which bore his name; but on inspection he noticed that they were written by another person.
Recruits from British Prisoners.
Levine went on to tell Price that they were permitted to send recruits to England for propaganda purposes, and that the idea was that they should be paid while doing so, and that they should be provided with funds.
The way Levine spoke led Price to think that Levine really thought that he was making a revolution in England.

放弃了尝试，通过给每人一堆宣传文献将他们打发走。普赖斯离开大楼时，看见并认出的一名来自阿尔汉格尔斯克的英国士兵，他带着一捆文件，似乎受雇从事文书工作。

特别信使。
不信任邮政系统。
尽管当局正竭尽全力扼杀布尔什维克主义学说在本国的传播，但他们自然面临许多困难。
布尔什维克分子出于显而易见的原因，不利用邮政和电报等普通通讯渠道，试图用其有害的学说渗透本国的劳工阶层，而是不遗余力地派遣特别信使在欧洲大陆与英国之间往返。
这位高级官员说：“前几天，我们得到情报，有一批人通过与船员的串通，作为偷渡者从鹿特丹过来，船员在每起案件中可获得5英镑。”
在伦敦东区被发现。
“我们设法找回了大约十一名这样的人，我们在伦敦东区发现了他们。
“他们都是知道自己无法获得护照的人，由鹿特丹的一个犹太组织派遣过来，该组织试图帮助人们逃避护照规定。
“我们也知道，俄罗斯和匈牙利的主要布尔什维克分子最近一直试图将代理人引入本国。如果说我们总能在他们登陆前找到他们，那是无稽之谈，有时我们只有在某些布尔什维克材料被广泛散布并引起我们注意后，才得知这一事实。
伦敦的组织。
“伦敦有一个特定的组织，协助传播从国外带来的这些革命观点。我们有时会以某人散发的传单形式发现这一点，或者它出现在某些具有极端倾向组织的通告中。
“在某些人作为偷渡者进入并离开本国后，我们也获得了情报。目前局势的唯一替代方案是在港口实施如此严格的检查，以至于我们可以限制旅行，从而迅速将这些个人彻底摧毁。
“但在当前关头，如果不损害国家利益，就无法对旅行施加很大的限制。人们写信说‘警察为什么不阻止这一切’，但在目前条件下，这并不容易。
“另一种常见的做法是试图雇用一艘驶往本国的船只上的海员作为信使。
‘你们完全掌控了局势吗？’《晚旗报》记者问道。
‘掌控局势的是英国民众，他们在了解事实后总能做出正确的决定，’这是回答。

红色分子的机会就在现在。
局势从未如此具有革命性。
“局势从未如此具有深刻的革命性，也从未像现在这样有利于建立一个新世界。”俄罗斯作家高尔基最近如是宣称，这无疑表达了共产主义者的感受，他们视欧洲目前的混乱和无序为他们的机会。

一名神秘女子。
布尔什维克宣传体系的首脑。
俄罗斯的阴谋。
英国囚犯中的阴谋故事。
日复一日，布尔什维克企图将欧洲，特别是英国，陷入“红色”革命者阴险罗网的广泛性质正在被揭露。
今天，《晚旗报》能够向读者提供这一几乎遍布全球的大阴谋的确凿证据。这些事实来自苏格兰场的一位最高级官员，他对局势的了解是第一手的，其事实经过充分证实。
一位高级官员今天说：“抓获这些布尔什维克使者极其困难。有人大声疾呼，护照和港口限制正在扼杀英国贸易。这其中有很多真实成分。
“虽然每天往返欧洲大陆的交通量非常大，但几乎不可能对每个人进行拦截、搜查和盘问，因为我们现在并非处于战争状态。
“即使是最看似信誉良好的旅行者，也总是有可能在口袋或衬里里携带几百英镑的钞票，并能对其持有这笔钱及其最终去向给出令人满意的解释；但是，当我们得知某些人入境时，如那名来自挪威的年轻人一案，我们会对他们保持警惕，并采取相应行动。”

布尔什维克分子试图贿赂军士
若他传播其学说，则提供优厚报酬。
此前已披露细节，说明年轻的挪威人扎哈里亚森如何躲过港口的监视，并将6000英镑提供给革命者使用。表面上，他是来研究社会状况的，并伪装成代表一家挪威报纸的记者。
然而，事实仍然是，他首先拜访的是持有极端观点的人，特别是在一个案例中，拜访了一名毫不掩饰其革命倾向的人。此外，他还携带了一批在战争期间涉嫌从事德国间谍活动的人员的地址。
来自布尔什维克中心。
但必须明确的是，这些名字不包括本国任何工党领袖，或实际上任何负责任的人士。然而，他来自挪威主要的布尔什维克中心这一事实，足以表明其使命的一般宗旨。
接着是发现“中央工人苏维埃委员会纲领”的披露，该纲领在十五点中将第三点列为：“全体劳动人口的军队是一支红军”，并以“万岁

以及俄罗斯本身，均在列宁和托洛茨基的直接命令下。
不幸的是，她尚未冒险尝试进入本国，从当局的角度来看，这是一种遗憾。但她被称为最暴力的“红色”分子之一，且已知在俄罗斯革命中，一些女性比男性更加嗜血和危险。
布尔什维克分子以迂回的方式工作，为了推进其邪恶计划，甚至不惜试图收买在俄罗斯的英国囚犯。

军士的陈述
试图使其成为布尔什维克代理人。
据《晚旗报》获悉，当局刚刚获得了机枪团普赖斯军士的宣誓陈述，他在俄罗斯作为战俘期间，曾被通过贿赂和晋升承诺，要求成为在英国的布尔什维克代理人。普赖斯军士的陈述如下：—
去年五月初，我作为一名劳工工作，当时他被带到一名名叫莱文的犹太人面前。
普赖斯面对一些书面材料，并被询问是否有人向他提议返回英国。他坦率承认布尔什维克分子曾接触过他，其中他注意到一些带有他名字的材料；但在检查时，他注意到这些是由另一个人书写的。
从英国囚犯中招募人员。
莱文继续告诉普赖斯，他们被允许向英国派遣人员进行宣传，并且想法是他们在这样做时应获得报酬，并为他们提供资金。
莱文的说话方式让普赖斯认为，莱文真的以为他正在英国发动革命。

Tsingtao, 19.3.32
Dear Sir,
I am very pleased to tell you that I have found my
wife in Tsingtao and everything is all right.
I wish to thank you very much for your assistance in
this matter and should I at any future period know of anyone
requiring assistance in your line of business will recommend you.
Will you please return photographs etc to the Internatio-
nal Export Co, Tientsin.
Thanking you again
Yours sincerely
F.V.Cleave

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
（印：SHANG... File No. ... C. & ... SECTION 2 ... No. ... 3708 ... Date March 14, 1932）

REPORT

Subject (in full)....Whereabouts of Mrs A.Y.Cleave.

Made by.........D.S.Prokofiev................Forwarded by......（签名）......

With reference to the attached letter of February
22,1932 from Mr F.V.Cleave, Tientsin, on the subject of his wife,
Mrs A.Y.Cleave, diligent enquiries have failed to elicit any in-
formation regarding the presence in Shanghai of this lady who is
believed to have left Tsingtao on February 11,1932,ostensibly to
proceed to this city via Tsinan - Fukow and river steamer.

Enquiries made in connection with this matter at the
local British Consulate-General, offices of shipping companies
maintaining passenger service on the Yangtsze river, the China
National Aviation Corporation, boardinghouse sections of both
the Settlement and French police, hotels and leading dressmakers
salons, have been without result.

A. Prokofiev
D. S.

Officer i/c Special Branch.

声称经济南、浦口并乘内河轮船前往本市。

就此事项在当地英国总领事馆、维持长江客运服务的轮船公司办事处、

酒店以及主要裁缝沙龙进行的查询，均无结果。

A. Prokofiev
警探

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL
& S.P. REGISTRY
S.B.D. 3308
1334
International Export Co.
Tientsin
China.
Feb. 22. 1932.

The Capt Supt.
Municipal Police
Shanghai.

Dear Sir.
I hope you will excuse me for
writing to you at such a busy time about
what you may think a trivial matter
but is worrying me a great deal.
To the best of my knowledge my
wife left Tsingtao (where she had been visiting
her sister) on Feb 11th. to go to Shanghai
via Tsinanfu, Pukow, & River Steamer.
Since then neither her sister or myself
have heard anything of her.
She had left me a week previously
in good spirits and friendly mood stating
she would return on the 17th.
She had about $100 and a fair
size suitcase and hat box, was dressed
in a long Blue Pilot Cloth Coat and
close fitting light Brown hat. She also had
a waist length, Young Sable fur, jacket in
her bag which she would probably wear
pages.zh:
上海公共租界工部局
& S.P. 登记处
S.B.D. 3308
1334
国际出口公司
天津
中国。
1932年2月22日。

致巡捕房总巡
公共租界警务处
上海。

尊敬的先生：
希望您能原谅我在如此繁忙的时候给您写信，谈论一件您可能认为琐碎
但令我非常担忧的事情。
据我所知，我的妻子于2月11日离开青岛（她在那里探望她的姐姐），
经济南府、浦口，并乘内河轮船前往上海。
此后，她的姐姐和我都没有听到她的任何消息。
她在一周前离开我时情绪良好，态度友好，表示将于17日返回。
她带了大约100美元和一个中等大小的手提箱及帽盒，身穿一件
蓝色飞行员呢长外套，头戴一顶紧身的浅棕色帽子。她的包里还有一件
腰长的年轻紫貂皮夹克，她可能会穿着

pages.en:
in Shanghai with a Red Hat which she
also had with her.
Height 5' 4" weight 140-145.
Hair dark Brown, not long, not short.
Before marriage was a dress designer
& cutter & would probably get a position
in a Salon with little difficulty
Has no friends in Shanghai to my
knowledge perhaps a couple of
acquaintances.
Known to all her Russian Friends
etc as Annayakovlina,
Name before marriage Anna Jeanette
Bergoltz
In Possession of British Passport No
63 issued in Tientsin July 5. 1928.
Speaks English fairly well.
I would be greatly obliged if in
the event of you finding her you did not
let her know anything but sent her
address to me and I will immediately
come down to her.
Thanking you in anticipation
Yours gratefully.
H. V. Cleave

Enclosed { Copy of her Passport Photo
       { also snapshot taken 3 weeks ago with
         myself..
pages.zh:
在上海，戴着一顶红帽子，该帽子也随她携带。
身高5英尺4英寸，体重140-145磅。
头发深褐色，不长不短。
婚前是一名服装设计师及裁剪师，很可能不难在一家时装沙龙找到职位。
据我所知，她在上海没有朋友，或许只有几位熟人。
她的所有俄罗斯朋友等均称其为 Annayakovlina，
婚前姓名为 Anna Jeanette Bergoltz。
持有英国护照，号码63，1928年7月5日于天津签发。
英语说得相当好。
若贵方找到她，恳请勿向她透露任何信息，仅将其地址告知我，我将立即前去见她。
预致谢意。
此致
敬礼。
H. V. Cleave
